newsitem.title: INDIA: India's EIH to double hotel rooms by 2000.
newsitem.headline: India's EIH to double hotel rooms by 2000.

text.p: India's East India Hotels Ltd (EIH) said on Tuesday it would invest 4.5 billion rupees ($125.6 million) to double its hotel room capacity to over 3,300 by 2000.

"The government expects 5 million foreign visitors by 2000. Even if hotel room capacity is doubled, we are likely to fall short," EIH's vice-chairman and managing director P.R.S. Oberoi told reporters after the company's 47th annual general meeting.
He outlined the company's expansion plans, spearheaded by a 325 room luxury hotel in Madras scheduled to open in 1998.
Construction had begun on a luxury hotel in Agra, and one in the state of Himachal Pradesh.
Oberoi said EIH Limited had formed a joint venture with Hong Kong's CCA International Ltd last month to develop and manage private clubs and resorts in India.
EIH had invested $8.06 million in the equity capital of its fully-owned subsiduary, EIH International Limited, which would use these funds to invest in hotel projects overseas, he said.

Currently, EIH International was in the process of constructing luxury resorts in Mauritius, Bali and on Egypt's Red Sea coast, Oberoi added. EIH's luxury resort in Lombok, Indonesia opened in January 1997.
